metadata.title: On the Multilinear Restriction and Kakeya conjectures
metadata.authors: Jonathan Bennett, Anthony Carbery, Terence Tao

nodes.name: Extension operator
nodes.statement: For a smooth parametrisation $\Sigma : U \to \R^d$ of a $(d-1)$-dimensional submanifold of $\R^d$, the extension operator $\ex$ is defined by $\ex g(\xi) := \int_U g(x) e^{i\xi \cdot \Sigma(x)} dx$ for $g \in L^1(U)$, $\xi \in \R^d$.

nodes.name: Transversality (spanning) condition
nodes.statement: For each $1 \leq j \leq d$, with $Y_j(x) := \bigwedge_{k=1}^{d-1} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_k} \Sigma_j(x)$, the spanning condition is $\det(Y_1(x^{(1)}),\ldots,Y_d(x^{(d)})) \geq \nu$ for all $x^{(j)} \in U_j$.

nodes.name: Smoothness condition
nodes.statement: $\|\Sigma_j\|_{C^2(U_j)} \leq A$ for all $1 \leq j \leq d$.

nodes.name: $\delta$-tube
nodes.statement: A $\delta$-tube is a rectangular box $T$ in $\R^d$ with $d-1$ sides of length $\delta$ and one side of length $1$; such tubes have volume $|T| \sim \delta^{d-1}$.

nodes.name: Transversal family of tubes
nodes.statement: Families $\T_1,\ldots,\T_d$ of $\delta$-tubes in $\R^d$ are transversal if for each $j$, the long sides of tubes in $\T_j$ point in directions in a sufficiently small neighbourhood of $e_j \in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$.

nodes.name: Loomis--Whitney matrix
nodes.statement: For $1 \leq j \leq d$, the $j$th Loomis--Whitney matrix $A_j^0$ is the orthogonal projection onto the hyperplane $\{x \in \R^d : x_j = 0\}$; equivalently, the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries all $1$ except the $j$th, which is $0$.

nodes.name: Positive semi-definite ordering
nodes.statement: $A \leq_{pd} B$ iff $B-A$ is positive semi-definite; $A <_{pd} B$ iff $B-A$ is positive definite.

nodes.name: Sliding gaussian quantity $f_j(t,x)$
nodes.statement: $f_j(t,x) := \int_{\R^d} e^{-\pi \langle A_j(x - v_j t), (x - v_j t) \rangle} d\mu_j(v_j)$, with $t$ interpreted as a time variable and $v_j$ as velocities.

nodes.name: Monotone quantity $Q_p(t)$
nodes.statement: $Q_p(t) := \int_{\R^d} \prod_{j=1}^n f_j(t,x)^{p_j} dx$ for exponent vector $p = (p_1,\ldots,p_n) \in (0,\infty)^n$.

nodes.name: Joint
nodes.statement: A joint is a point in $\R^3$ contained in at least one triple $(l,l',l'')$ of concurrent, non-coplanar lines from a collection $L$.

nodes.name: $\theta$-transverse joint
nodes.statement: Three concurrent lines $l,l',l''$ are $\theta$-transverse if the parallelopiped generated by their unit direction vectors has volume at least $\theta$. A $\theta$-transverse joint is a point contained in at least one such triple.

nodes.name: Variable-coefficient operator $S_\lambda$
nodes.statement: For smooth phase $\Phi : \R^{d-1} \times \R^d \to \R$ and cut-off $\psi$, $S_\lambda g(\xi) := \int_{\R^{d-1}} e^{i\lambda \Phi(x,\xi)} \psi(x,\xi) g(x) dx$, with vector field $X(\Phi) := \bigwedge_{k=1}^{d-1} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_k} \nabla_\xi \Phi$.

nodes.name: Curvy tube $T_j$
nodes.statement: $T_j := \{\xi \in \R^d : |\nabla_x \Phi_j(a,\xi) - \omega| \leq \delta,\ (a,\xi) \in \supp(\psi_j)\}$ for some $a,\omega \in \R^{d-1}$; an $O(\delta)$-neighbourhood of a smooth curve.

nodes.name: $\re^*$ and $\ka^*$ schemata
nodes.statement: $\re^*(p\times\cdots\times p \to q;\alpha)$ denotes $\|\prod_j \ex_j g_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))} \leq C R^\alpha \prod_j \|g_j\|_{L^p(U_j)}$; $\ka^*(1\times\cdots\times 1 \to q;\alpha)$ denotes $\|\prod_j \sum_{T_j \in \T_j}\chi_{T_j}\|_{q/d} \leq C \delta^{-\alpha}\prod_j(\delta^{d/q}\#\T_j)$.

nodes.name: Linear Restriction Conjecture
nodes.statement: If $S$ has everywhere non-vanishing gaussian curvature, $q > \tfrac{2d}{d-1}$, and $p' \leq \tfrac{d-1}{d+1} q$, then $\|\ex g\|_{L^q(\R^d)} \leq C\|g\|_{L^p(U)}$.
conclusions: $\|\ex g\|_{L^q(\R^d)} \leq C\|g\|_{L^p(U)}$ for all $g \in L^p(U)$, with $C$ depending only on $d, \Sigma$

nodes.name: Multilinear Restriction Conjecture
nodes.statement: Under the spanning and smoothness conditions, for $q \geq \tfrac{2d}{d-1}$ and $p' \leq \tfrac{d-1}{d}q$, $\|\prod_{j=1}^d \ex_j g_j\|_{L^{q/d}(\R^d)} \leq C \prod_{j=1}^d \|g_j\|_{L^p(U_j)}$.

nodes.name: Linear Kakeya Conjecture
nodes.statement: For $\tfrac{d}{d-1} < q \leq \infty$, $\|\sum_{T \in \T} \chi_T\|_{L^q(\R^d)} \leq C\delta^{(d-1)/q}(\#\T)^{1/q}$, with $C$ independent of $\delta$ and $\T$.
assumptions: $\T$ is a collection of $\delta$-tubes with $\delta$-separated orientations on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$

nodes.name: Multilinear Kakeya Conjecture
nodes.statement: For transversal families $\T_1,\ldots,\T_d$ of $\delta$-tubes and $\tfrac{d}{d-1} \leq q \leq \infty$, $\|\prod_{j=1}^d (\sum_{T_j \in \T_j}\chi_{T_j})\|_{L^{q/d}(\R^d)} \leq C \prod_j (\delta^{d/q}\#\T_j)$.

nodes.name: Loomis--Whitney inequality
nodes.statement: For projections $\pi_j(x) := (x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1},x_{j+1},\ldots,x_d)$, $\int_{\R^d} \prod_{j=1}^d f_j(\pi_j(x))\, dx \leq \prod_{j=1}^d \|f_j\|_{d-1}$ for all $f_j \in L^{d-1}(\R^{d-1})$.

nodes.name: Near-optimal multilinear Kakeya
nodes.statement: For $\tfrac{d}{d-1} < q \leq \infty$ there is $C$ independent of $\delta$ and transversal families, such that $\|\prod_j \sum_{T_j \in \T_j} \chi_{T_j}\|_{L^{q/d}(\R^d)} \leq C\prod_j(\delta^{d/q}\#\T_j)$. Moreover, an $\delta^{-\eps}$-loss endpoint inequality holds at $q = \tfrac{d}{d-1}$.

nodes.name: Near-optimal multilinear restriction
nodes.statement: For $\eps > 0$, $q \geq \tfrac{2d}{d-1}$, $p' \leq \tfrac{d-1}{d}q$, $\|\prod_j \ex_j g_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))} \leq C R^\eps \prod_j \|g_j\|_{L^p(U_j)}$ for all $g_j \in L^p(U_j)$ and $R \geq 1$.

nodes.name: $n$-linear Kakeya in $\R^d$
nodes.statement: For $3 \leq n \leq d$ and $\tfrac{n}{n-1} < q \leq \infty$, transversal families $\T_1,\ldots,\T_n$ of $\delta$-tubes in $\R^d$ satisfy $\|\prod_{j=1}^n \sum_{T_j \in \T_j} \chi_{T_j}\|_{L^{q/n}(\R^d)} \leq C \prod_{j=1}^n (\delta^{d/q} \#\T_j)$.

nodes.name: Variable-coefficient multilinear restriction
nodes.statement: Under the diffeomorphism transversality \eqref{difftrans} and uniform smoothness \eqref{sm}, for $\eps > 0$, $q \geq \tfrac{2d}{d-1}$, $p' \leq \tfrac{d-1}{d}q$, $\|\prod_j S_\lambda^{(j)} g_j\|_{L^{q/d}(\R^d)} \leq C_\eps \lambda^\eps \prod_j \lambda^{-d/q}\|g_j\|_{L^p(\R^{d-1})}$.

nodes.name: Variable-coefficient multilinear Kakeya
nodes.statement: Under \eqref{difftrans} and \eqref{sm}, for $\eps > 0$ and $q \geq \tfrac{d}{d-1}$, $\|\prod_j \sum_{T_j \in \T_j}\chi_{T_j}\|_{L^{q/d}(\R^d)} \leq C_\eps \delta^{-\eps}\prod_j(\delta^{d/q}\#\T_j)$.

nodes.name: Joints estimate
nodes.statement: For any $0 < \theta \leq 1$ and configuration $L$ of $n$ lines in $\R^3$, the number of $\theta$-transverse joints is $O_\eps(n^{3/2+\eps}\theta^{-1/2-\eps})$ for any $\eps > 0$.
assumptions: $L$ is a collection of $n$ lines in $\R^3$

nodes.name: Multilinear restriction $\Leftrightarrow$ multilinear Kakeya
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\eps \geq 0$ and $\tfrac{2d}{d-1} \leq q \leq \infty$: $\re^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\alpha) + \ka^*(1\times\cdots\times 1 \to \tfrac{q}{2};\eps) \implies \re^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{\eps}{4})$.

nodes.name: Loomis--Whitney monotonicity
nodes.statement: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be positive semi-definite real symmetric $d\times d$ matrices and $\mu_j$ finite compactly supported positive Borel measures. If $p \in (0,\infty)^n$ with $\sum_j p_j A_j$ non-singular and $A_j \leq_{pd} \sum_k p_k A_k$ for all $j$, then $Q_p(t)$ is non-increasing in $t$.
assumptions: $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ positive semi-definite real symmetric $d\times d$ matrices
$\mu_j$ finite compactly supported positive Borel measures on $\R^d$

nodes.name: Loomis--Whitney bound at $t=1$
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Proposition~\ref{lwmon}, $\int \prod_j f_j(1,x)^{p_j} dx \leq \int \prod_j f_j(0,x)^{p_j} dx = (\det A_*)^{-1/2} \prod_j \|\mu_j\|^{p_j}$ where $A_* = \sum_k p_k A_k$.

nodes.name: Approximate monotonicity (perturbed Loomis--Whitney)
nodes.statement: Let $M_1,\ldots,M_n$ be psd symmetric $d\times d$ matrices, $p$ with $\sum_j p_j M_j$ non-singular and $\sum_j p_j M_j >_{pd} M_l$ for all $l$. If $\Omega_j$ are pairs $(A_j,v_j)$ with $\|A_j^{1/2} - M_j^{1/2}\| \leq \eps$ and $\eps$ small enough, then $\int \prod_j f_j(t,x)^{p_j} dx \leq (1+O(\eps))\int \prod_j f_j(0,x)^{p_j} dx$ for all $t \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Perturbed Loomis--Whitney bound
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Proposition~\ref{wowgen}, $\int \prod_j f_j(1,x)^{p_j} dx \leq (1 + O(\eps))(\det M_*)^{-1/2}\prod_j \|\mu_j\|^{p_j}$ where $M_* = \sum_k p_k M_k$.

nodes.name: Uncertainty principle for $\re^*$
nodes.statement: $\re^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\alpha)$ is true iff $\|\prod_j \widehat{f}_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))} \leq C R^{\alpha - d/2}\prod_j \|f_j\|_2$ for all $R \geq 1$ and $f_j$ supported in $A_j^R = \Sigma_j(U_j) + O(R^{-1})$.
conclusions: $\re^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\alpha) \iff \|\prod_j \widehat{f}_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))} \leq C R^{\alpha-d/2}\prod_j \|f_j\|_2$ for $f_j$ supported in $A_j^R$

nodes.name: Formula for $S$ at $\B_j = M_j^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $p_1,\ldots,p_n > 0$, $S(p,(\E((M_j^{1/2},\w_j)^{\otimes m})))$ equals $\det M_* \{ \sum_j p_j \|\E(\w_j)\|^2 + \sum_j p_j \E\langle (I-M_j^{1/2}M_*^{-1}M_j^{1/2})(\w_j-\E\w_j), (\w_j-\E\w_j)\rangle - \|M_*^{-1/2}\sum_j p_j M_j^{1/2}\E(\w_j)\|^2 \}$.

nodes.name: Rigidity of rank-$(d-1)$ Loomis--Whitney configurations
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 3$. If $A_1,\ldots,A_d$ are psd $d\times d$ rank-$(d-1)$ matrices whose kernels span and $\tfrac{1}{d-1}(A_1+\cdots+A_d) \geq A_1,\ldots,A_d$, then $A_d$ is uniquely determined by $A_1,\ldots,A_{d-1}$.

nodes.name: Failure of monotonicity at endpoint
nodes.statement: For $j=1,\ldots,d$ let $W_j$ be a set of psd rank-$(d-1)$ matrices with kernels spanning, $\mu_j$ measures on $W_j\times\R^d$, and $p = (1/(d-1),\ldots,1/(d-1))$. If $Q_p(1) \leq Q_p(0)$ for all such $\mu_j$, then either $d=2$ or each $W_j$ is a singleton with $\tfrac{1}{d-1}(A_1+\cdots+A_d) \geq A_l$ for all $l$.
conclusions: either $d=2$ or each $W_j$ is a singleton and $\tfrac{1}{d-1}\sum A_j \geq A_l$ for all $l$

nodes.name: Curvy Kakeya bootstrapping
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\eps > 0$ and $q > \tfrac{d}{d-1}$, $\ka_c^*(1\times\cdots\times 1 \to q;\alpha) + \ka^*(1\times\cdots\times 1\to q;\eps) \implies \ka_c^*(1\times\cdots\times 1 \to q;\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{\eps}{2})$.

nodes.name: Curvy restriction bootstrapping
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\eps,\eps_0 > 0$ and $q > \tfrac{2d}{d-1}$, $\re_c^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\alpha) + \ka_c^*(1\times\cdots\times 1 \to \tfrac{q}{2};\eps) \implies \re_c^*(2\times\cdots\times 2 \to q;\tfrac{\alpha}{2}+\tfrac{\eps}{4}+\eps_0)$.

nodes.name: Polynomial extrapolation
nodes.statement: If $f_1,\ldots,f_n: \R^d \to \R$ are bounded non-negative measurable with $\prod f_j$ rapidly decreasing, and $G_1,G_2$ are polynomials in $p$ with measurable coefficients of polynomial growth, then $\int G_1(p,x)\prod f_j^{p_j} dx = \int G_2(p,x)\prod f_j^{p_j} dx$ for all $p \in \N^n$ implies the same for all $p \in (0,\infty)^n$.
assumptions: $G_1,G_2$ polynomial in $p$ with measurable polynomial-growth coefficients

nodes.name: Loomis--Whitney gaussian reformulation
nodes.statement: $\|\prod_j \sum_{v_j \in V_j} e^{-\pi\langle A_j^0(\cdot - v_j),(\cdot-v_j)\rangle}\|_{L^{1/(d-1)}(\R^d)} \leq C \prod_j \#V_j$.

nodes.name: Formula for $G(p,t,x)$
nodes.statement: $G(p,t,x) = \sum_j p_j \E\langle(A_j - A_j A_*^{-1} A_j)(\v_j-\E\v_j),(\v_j-\E\v_j)\rangle + \sum_j p_j \langle A_j(\E\v_j - \E\overline{\v}),(\E\v_j - \E\overline{\v})\rangle$.

nodes.name: Choice of $v_0$ killing the bad term
Proof of Proposition MRiffMK
nodes.statement: By Lemma uncertainty, reduce to estimating $\|\prod_j \widehat{f}_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))}$; introduce $L^1$-normalised modulated bumps $\phi_{R^{1/2}}^x$, average over $x$, decompose $A_j^R$ into $R^{-1/2}$-discs, and apply hypothesis $\ka^*$ via Plancherel.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition lwmon
nodes.statement: Treat integer $p$: differentiate $Q_p(t)$, complete the square, identify weighted variance $\delta$, take expectation with carefully chosen random variables, manipulate via independence/symmetry, obtain manifestly non-negative $G(p,t,x)$, and extend to non-integer $p$ via the extrapolation Lemma densitycor.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition wowgen
nodes.statement: Replace $Q_p$ by weighted $\tilde Q_p$ with extra factor $\det A_*$ to render expressions polynomial; differentiate, exploit Galilean invariance, choose $v_0$ to kill the unfavourable term; apply Lemma formulaforS and extrapolation; conclude positivity for $\eps$ small.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem joints-thm
nodes.statement: First handle $\theta \sim 1$ via covering of $\mathbb{S}^2$ by caps and applying Theorem kakthm to associated tube families. Then handle small $\theta$ by dyadic decomposition into $(\alpha,\beta)$-transverse triples and apply rescaling/Cauchy--Schwarz arguments for $\alpha\sim 1$ and small $\alpha$ separately.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma notmonlemma
nodes.statement: By [BCCT, Prop 3.6], the rank-$(d-1)$ matrices factor as $A_j = D^* P_j D$ with $P_j$ projections summing to $(d-1) I_d$. Show $\ker P_j$ are pairwise orthogonal, so up to basis change $P_j = A_j^0$. Any other invertible $\tilde D$ giving the same first $d-1$ matrices is forced to act diagonally with $\pm 1$ entries; hence $A_d$ is determined.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition prokak
nodes.statement: Tile $\R^d$ by cubes of side $\sqrt\delta$; restrict each curvy tube to a cube and observe these are $O(\delta)\times\cdots\times O(\sqrt\delta)$ rectangular tubes; apply $\ka^*(\cdot;\eps)$ on each; reassemble via averaging and the dilation $\widetilde T_j$ argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition prorest
nodes.statement: Wavepacket-decompose $g_j$ on $\sqrt{1/\lambda}$-cubes $Q$, localise $S_\lambda^{(j)} e_{Q,\ell}$ to curvy tubes $R_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}$ via integration by parts; estimate principal term using $\re_c^*(\cdot;\alpha)$ + $\ka_c^*(\cdot;\eps)$; bound error terms by standard decay.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma formulaforS
nodes.statement: For integer $p$, expand $S$ via \eqref{Sm-form} and \eqref{deltam-poly-2} with $\B_j = M_j^{1/2}$, use $\adj(M_*)=\det(M_*)M_*^{-1}$, exploit independence/symmetry, and rearrange to the claimed form. Apply Lemma densitycor for non-integer $p$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma densitycor
nodes.statement: Reduce to $G_2 = 0$ and $\|f_j\|_\infty = 1$. Approximate $\phi_p(t)=\prod t_j^{p_j}$ by polynomials vanishing on coordinate axes in a $C^N$-norm; apply hypothesis to each polynomial; control residuals by integrability of $\tilde w_\alpha$ when all $\alpha_j\geq 1$ and Newton-Leibniz-type bounds otherwise.

nodes.name: Reduction to endpoint $p=2$, $q=2d/(d-1)$
nodes.statement: By multilinear interpolation and H\"older, Conjecture MLRC reduces to the endpoint $L^2$ estimate $\|\prod_j \ex_j g_j\|_{L^{2/(d-1)}(\R^d)} \leq C \prod_j \|g_j\|_{L^2(U_j)}$.

nodes.name: MLRC generalises Loomis--Whitney
nodes.statement: If the $\Sigma_j$ are linear, by Plancherel the conjectured endpoint inequality is equivalent (with appropriate constant) to the classical Loomis--Whitney inequality \eqref{clw}.

nodes.name: Brascamp--Lieb connection
nodes.statement: Variants of Proposition lwmon and Corollary usemon1, by the authors and M. Christ, lead to new proofs of Lieb's theorem on gaussian exhaustion of Brascamp--Lieb inequalities.

nodes.name: Possible extension to linear Kakeya
nodes.statement: Variants of these techniques may lead to progress on the linear Kakeya conjecture; counterexamples (if any) would have to be ``non-transverse" or ``plany".

nodes.name: Lattice configuration achieving $\sim n^{3/2}$ joints
nodes.statement: Lines parallel to the coordinate axes with two coordinates fixed in $\{1,\ldots,\sqrt n\}$ yield at least $\sim n^{3/2}$ joints, providing a lower bound matched (up to logs) by Theorem joints-thm.

nodes.name: Expand $Q_p(t)$ for integer $p$
nodes.statement: For $p \in \N^n$, expand $Q_p(t) = \int \prod_j f_j^{p_j} dx$ as a multiple integral over $(\R^d)^{p_1}\times\cdots\times(\R^d)^{p_n}$ with the gaussian kernel.

nodes.name: Complete the square and compute $Q_p'(t)$
nodes.statement: Complete the square to write $\sum_{j,k}\langle A_j(x-v_{j,k}t),(x-v_{j,k}t)\rangle = \langle A_*(x-\bar v t),(x-\bar v t)\rangle + \delta t^2$; differentiate $Q_p$ to obtain $Q_p'(t) = -2\pi t \int \delta \prod_j f_j^{p_j} dx$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic reformulation via expectation
nodes.statement: Introduce random variables $\v_j$ with density $e^{-\pi\langle A_j(x-v_j t),(x-v_j t)\rangle}d\mu_j(v_j)/f_j(t,x)$ and write $Q_p'(t) = -2\pi t \int \E(\delta) \prod_j f_j^{p_j} dx$.

nodes.name: Manifestly non-negative form for $G(p,t,x)$
nodes.statement: Use independence and symmetry to rewrite $\E(\delta)$ as $G(p,t,x)$ which is a sum of two non-negative quadratic forms when $A_* \geq_{pd} A_j$ for all $j$, hence $Q_p'(t) \leq 0$.

nodes.name: Extrapolate from integer to real $p$
nodes.statement: Multiply $Q_p'(t)$ and the formula for $G$ by $\det A_*$ to make polynomial in $p$; apply Lemma densitycor to extend the identity from $p \in \N^n$ to $p \in (0,\infty)^n$.

nodes.name: Define modified $\tilde Q_p$ with $\det(A_*)$ weight
nodes.statement: Replace $Q_p$ by $\tilde Q_p$ which inserts factor $\det(A_*)$ inside; this avoids $A_*^{-1}$ and yields a polynomial expression in $\A_{j,k}$.

nodes.name: Compare $Q_p$ and $\tilde Q_p$
nodes.statement: Since $A_* = M_* + O(\eps)$, $\det A_* = \det M_* + O(\eps)$, so $Q_p(t) = (1+O(\eps))\det(M_*)^{-1} \tilde Q_p(t)$ for integer $p$, extended to all $p$ by extrapolation.

nodes.name: Differentiate $\tilde Q_p$ and apply Galilean invariance
nodes.statement: Compute $\tilde Q_p'(t)$ via completing the square; observe $\delta$ is unchanged under $\v_{j,k}\to\v_{j,k}-v_0$ for any deterministic field $v_0$; multiply by $\det \A_*$ to obtain a polynomial.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma formulaforS
nodes.statement: Use Lemma formulaforS to obtain a closed-form expression for $S(p,(\E((M_j^{1/2},\w_j)^{\otimes m})))$, isolating the unfavourable last term $\|M_*^{-1/2}\sum p_j M_j^{1/2}\E\w_j\|^2$.

nodes.name: Choose $v_0$ to kill the unfavourable term
nodes.statement: Choose $v_0 = \E(\sum p_j M_j^{1/2}\A_j^{1/2})^{-1}\sum p_j \E(M_j^{1/2}\A_j^{1/2}\v_j)$ which makes $\sum p_j M_j^{1/2}\E(\w_j) = 0$.

nodes.name: Conclude positivity for small $\eps$
nodes.statement: Use $I-M_j^{1/2}M_*^{-1}M_j^{1/2}\geq_{pd} cI$ and $\|\w_j\|^2 \leq 2\|\w_j-\E\w_j\|^2 + 2\|\E\w_j\|^2$ to absorb the $O(\eps)$ error term and obtain $\E(\det\A_*\delta) \geq 0$ for $\eps$ small.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\theta \sim 1$ via cap covering
nodes.statement: Cover $\mathbb{S}^2$ by $O(1)$ caps $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ of width $\theta/1000$; for $\theta$-transverse triples, three cap indices form a transverse triple; reduce to bounding joints in each $L_i\times L_{i'}\times L_{i''}$.

nodes.name: Apply multilinear Kakeya in $\theta\sim 1$ case
nodes.statement: For each joint $p$, the indicator sums $\sum_{T_i\in\T_i}\chi_{T_i}\geq 1$ on $|x-p|<c\delta$. Since balls are disjoint, $\|\prod_i \sum\chi_{T_i}\|_{L^{q/3}}\geq c_q N^{3/q}\delta^{9/q}$; apply Theorem kakthm to get $N \leq C_q^{q/3} (\#L_i \#L_{i'}\#L_{i''})^{q/3}$, then $q\to 3/2$.

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition for small $\theta$
nodes.statement: Decompose into $(\alpha,\beta)$-transverse joints with $\theta^{1/2}\lesssim\alpha\lesssim 1$, $\beta\sim\theta/\alpha$. Suffices to show number of $(\alpha,\beta)$-transverse joints is $O_\eps(n^{3/2+\eps}(\beta/\alpha)^{-1/2+\eps})$.

nodes.name: Case $\alpha \sim 1$ via $\beta$-direction rescaling
nodes.statement: Take a $\beta$-net $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_K$, $K=O(1/\beta^2)$; assign each line to nearby $L_k$ or $L_k'$; dilate by $1/\beta$ in $\omega_k$ direction to reduce to the previously handled $c$-transverse case; conclude via Cauchy--Schwarz over $k$.

nodes.name: Case $\alpha$ small via bilinear rescaling
nodes.statement: Take an $\alpha$-net of directions; group lines into families $\tilde L_k$ within $O(\alpha)$ of each $\tilde\omega_k$; dilate by $1/\alpha$ orthogonal to $\tilde\omega_k$ to reduce to $\alpha\sim 1$ case; bound $\sum_k \#\tilde L_k \leq Cn$ since each line lies in $O(1)$ families.

nodes.name: Apply uncertainty principle (Lemma uncertainty)
nodes.statement: By Lemma uncertainty, it suffices to show $\|\prod_j \widehat{f}_j\|_{L^{q/d}(B(0,R))} \lesssim R^{\alpha/2+\eps/4-d/2}\prod_j \|f_j\|_{L^2(A_j^R)}$.

nodes.name: Modulated bump averaging
nodes.statement: Introduce $L^1$-normalised modulated bumps $\phi_{R^{1/2}}^x$, apply $\re^*$ hypothesis on $B(x,R^{1/2})$, and average over $x \in B(0,R)$ to obtain inequality \eqref{49}.

nodes.name: Disc decomposition and Plancherel
nodes.statement: Cover $A_j^R$ by $R^{-1/2}$-discs $\{\rho_j\}$ with bounded overlap; use Plancherel and pointwise comparability of $\widetilde f_{j,\rho_j}=f_{j,\rho_j}/\psi_{\rho_j}$ to relate $L^2$ norms to convolutions $|\widehat{\widetilde f}_{j,\rho_j}|^2 * \chi_{\rho_j^*}$.

nodes.name: Apply Kakeya hypothesis on dilated tubes
nodes.statement: Apply rescaled hypothesis $\ka^*(1\times\cdots\times 1\to q/2;\eps)$ in its $\eqref{Kalphasuper}$ form to the convolution expression to obtain the bound $R^{\alpha/2+\eps/4-d/2}\prod_j\|f_j\|_{L^2(A_j^R)}$.

nodes.name: Tile by $\sqrt{\delta}$-cubes
nodes.statement: Tile $\R^d$ by cubes $B$ of side $\sqrt\delta$; rewrite the LHS as $\sum_B \|\prod_j \sum\chi_{T_j\cap B}\|_{L^{q/d}}^{q/d}$.

nodes.name: Locally straighten tubes
nodes.statement: By smoothness of $\Phi_j$, each $T_j \cap B$ is contained in a rectangular $O(\delta)\times\cdots\times O(\sqrt\delta)$-tube; the $d$ families satisfy the transversality of $\ka^*$.

nodes.name: Apply $\ka^*$ on each cube and average
nodes.statement: Apply $\ka^*(1\times\cdots\times 1\to q;\eps)$ to each cube; relate the sum to dilated tubes $\widetilde T_j$ via averaging; apply hypothesis $\ka_c^*(\cdot;\alpha)$ to conclude.

nodes.name: Wavepacket decomposition
nodes.statement: Tile $\R^{d-1}$ by $\lambda^{-1/2}$-cubes $Q$ with smooth partition $\chi_Q$; expand $g_j = \sum_{Q,\ell} a_{Q,\ell}^{(j)} e_{Q,\ell}$ where $e_{Q,\ell}=\chi_Q(x)e^{i\ell\cdot x}$.

nodes.name: Localise $S_\lambda^{(j)} e_{Q,\ell}$ to curvy tubes
nodes.statement: Define curvy tubes $R_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}$ via $|\nabla_x \Phi_j(x_Q,\xi)-\ell|\leq\lambda^{-1/2+\eta}$. By integration by parts, $|S_\lambda^{(j)}e_{Q,\ell}(\xi)| \lesssim \lambda^{-M\eta-(d-1)/2}$ outside $R_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}$.

nodes.name: Triangle decomposition into principal $I$ and tail $I_P$
nodes.statement: Tile $\R^d$ by $\lambda^{-1/2}$-cubes $B$; for each $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ define $I_P$ summing only $(Q,\ell)$ with $R_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}\cap B = \emptyset$ for $j\in P$. Bound $\|\prod S_\lambda^{(j)}g_j\|_{q/d}\leq I + \sum_P I_P$.

nodes.name: Bound principal term $I$
nodes.statement: By rescaling $\re_c^*(\cdot;\alpha)$ and almost-orthogonality of $e_{Q,\ell}$, $I \lesssim \lambda^{\alpha/2-d^2/q-d(d-1)/4}\bigl(\sum_B \prod_j(\sum_{Q,\ell}|a_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}|^2 \chi_{R_{Q,\ell}^{(j)}}(\xi_B))^{q/(2d)}\bigr)^{d/q}$. Apply $\ka_c^*(\cdot;\eps)$ and Plancherel to get $I \lesssim \lambda^{\alpha/2+\eps/4+\eps_0}\prod\lambda^{-d/q}\|g_j\|_2$.

nodes.name: Bound tail terms $I_P$ via decay
nodes.statement: Use H\"older's inequality and decay estimate $|S_\lambda^{(j)}e_{Q,\ell}|\lesssim \lambda^{-N\eta-(d-1)/2}$ off the curvy tube to get $I_P \lesssim \lambda^{-N\eta}\prod_j\|g_j\|_2$, negligible.
